subject: do.parallel for Verisense step count algorithm

messages.author: b9400d58a0bfce63
messages.subject: do.parallel for Verisense step count algorithm
parts:
Hello,

In the github documentation for Patterson's Verisense step count algorithm, the instructions are clear in saying: "6. Ensure that do.parallel is set to False in the GGIR entry function". I would like to know whether this is still necessary in GGIR.

I ask because in the GGIR documentation for using external functions, it says the following: " Note that, do.parallel is set to FALSE. Unfortunately Python embedding with R package reticulate and multi-threading with R package foreach as used in GGIR do not combine well." This note of caution appears under the section for using an external Python function, whereas the Verisense step count algorithm is using an R external function.

Given the long runtimes necessary for GGIR part 1, being able to run in parallel makes a huge difference. Is there any way this is possible? Thank you in advance for the help and great package!

Thomas Kraft

messages.author: 5270e62a7d3ec577
messages.subject: Re: do.parallel for Verisense step count algorithm
parts:
Hi Thomas,

I have run this with do.parallel = T on several datasets and it's worked perfectly. I remember having the same query you have about a year ago, and decided to just go ahead and try it.

Thanks,
Ben
